threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 30 bus is a reliable option after 10 PM. That's a rookie mistake; the night buses are a whole different game.
Heard a guy on the 35 last night trying to impress a girl by claiming he lived in a 'penthouse'… it was just a flat over the shops on Coldharbour Lane.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids using the U-Bahn platform as a skate park while their parents chatted over coffee—just a regular Saturday.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a spontaneous techno party in a hidden backyard that turns into an open-air art gallery by morning.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate a BART delay—no stress, just a quick taco stop and a text to their boss about 'transit issues.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy holding a full pizza on the 47 bus, swaying with it while everyone else just stared. Classic Muni moment right there.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí but miss the hidden plazas where locals gather for vermut—way more authentic than any tourist trap.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones who still ask for a plastic bag at the market, unaware that you need to bring your own or pay for one.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pay for your coffee with cash and look surprised when your change is in coins. Everyone else is using contactless like it's second nature.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last Saturday; saw a bloke trying to barter a kebab for a seat. Driver just shook his head and laughed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The evening smell of grilled kebabs wafting from the corner stand while kids chase each other on the sidewalk, that’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous open-air techno raves in abandoned buildings here; it's not just a party, it's a Berlin ritual.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their tolerance for BART delays—baffled tourists are still on their phones trying to figure out the next bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 7 bus heading to a wedding. He said 'better late than never' as we all looked on. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas. In Gràcia, some of the best spots offer pintxos, and they're missing out by sticking to the familiar.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their confusion over which side of the street the tram stops on; locals glide right past without a second thought.
